title: Telecoms Regulatory Corpus — Ofcom & EECC
source: Ofcom (UK Office of Communications) / European Electronic Communications Code (EECC) / DCMS
description: Complete regulatory corpus for UK electronic communications and telecoms, covering Ofcom's General Conditions of Entitlement, the European Electronic Communications Code implementation in UK law, spectrum regulation, consumer protection, network security, and AI-specific telecoms obligations.
key_regulations: Communications Act 2003 (primary legislation creating Ofcom)
Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 (spectrum management)
European Electronic Communications Code (EECC) — Directive (EU) 2018/1972 — transposed into UK law via Electronic Communications (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 and subsequent amendments
Electronic Communications Code (ECC) — Schedule 3A to the Communications Act 2003 (operator rights to install infrastructure)
Electronic Communications (Security Measures) Regulations 2022 (Telecoms Security Regulations)
Telecommunications (Security) Act 2021
Ofcom General Conditions of Entitlement (GCE) — current consolidated version (2025)
Ofcom Universal Service Conditions — Minimum broadband (10 Mbps) and voice telephony
Ofcom Spectrum Framework: Award and licensing regulations for all spectrum bands
Network and Information Systems Regulations 2018/2025 (NIS — telecoms part)
DORA Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 — digital operational resilience for telecoms firms with financial services  activities
Data Retention and Investigatory Powers Act 2014 (as amended by Investigatory Powers Act 2016)
Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (PECR) — cookies, e-privacy, electronic marketing
General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and Data Protection Act 2018
Article 27 of EECC: End-user protection — contract rights, transparency, switching
Ofcom Net Neutrality Rules (Open Internet Access Regulations 2016, SI 2016/607)
EU Digital Markets Act — ex-ante regulation of very large online platforms intersecting with telecoms (extraterritorial for UK EU-facing operators)

EU AI Act 2024/1689 — Articles relevant to telecoms: Article 6(2) high-risk for telecoms customer-facing AI, Article 12 for technical documentation of AI-powered network optimisation, Article 50 transparency for AI-generated communications
Telecoms Code of Practice for vulnerable consumers (vulnerability manda under GCE condition C5)
UK Online Safety Act 2023 — user-to-user service duties for telecoms messaging services
compliance_requirements: General Conditions of Entitlement compliance: All 50+ conditions covering consumer protection (C1-C11), network access (C12-C19), numbering (C20-C27), and enforcement (C28-C50+)
Universal Service Obligation (USO): Provide affordable broadband (at least 10 Mbps) and voice telephony to any UK household upon reasonable request

Telecoms Security Framework (2022 Regulations): 13 high-level security measures including: network architecture, supply chain security (Section 5), security monitoring, testing (Section 6), incident management (Section 7 — reporting to NCSC/Ofcom within 24 hours for significant incidents), customer premises equipment security
Section 105 Code of Practice (Duty to notify Ofcom of security compromises — 72-hour notification)
Network and Information Systems (NIS) reporting: Telecoms providers classified as essential entities under UK NIS 2025 — 24-hour incident warning, 72-hour full report
Ofcom spectrum licence conditions: Spectrum fees (Annual Licence Fees — ALF or AIP), coverage obligations, interference management and complaint handling

Net neutrality compliance: No blocking, throttling, or discriminatory traffic management outside of GCE Condition C4 exceptions (court order, network integrity, congestion management with transparency)
Consumer contract transparency: Pre-contract information (GCE C1), annual summary (GCE C1A), contract renewal notification (GCE C1B), contract summary for vulnerable customers
Consumer switching: GCE C2 provides one-touch switching across fixed broadband and voice providers (One Touch Switch (OTS) scheme implemented since 2023)
Number portability (GCE C3): Mobile number portability within one working day
Special measures for vulnerable customers: GCE C5 — priority fault repair, accessible communications, debt management support, registration of customers with vulnerabilities

Billing and pricing transparency (GCE C4): Mid-contract price rise notification (30 days), in-contract price indexing transparency from January 2025 (Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024)
Wholesale access (GCE C12-C19): Openreach physical infrastructure access, duct and pole access, dark fibre, wholesale local access (WLA — FTTC/FTTP), Ethernet services
Emergency services access (GCE C6): E112 for mobile, ECS 112/999 emergency call routing
Directory enquiry services and subscriber databases (GCE C7-C8): End-user privacy at 1.23, correct directory listing for consumers
Data retention and lawful intercept: Investigatory Powers Act compliance for communications data retention, lawful intercept capability
Carbon reporting: SECR (Streamlined Energy and Carbon Reporting) for telecoms network operators
Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) for AI-driven network optimisation, customer analytics, and targeted marketing
Ofcom Accessibility Requirements: Communications services accessible to disabled end-users under Section 10 of the Act and GCE C5
Numbering administration: Compliance with National Numbering Scheme (NTS), OFCOM's number allocation plan, number conservation
penalties: Ofcom financial penalty: Up to 10% of applicable turnover for any breach of General Conditions, Spectrum Licence, or Security Regulations — no upper limit in Communications Act 2003 (Section 392)
Ofcom notice period penalty scheme for persistent consumer law breaches: Daily penalty up to £20,000 for ongoing non-compliance with enforcement notices
Telecoms Security Regulation penalties: Ofcom can impose fines up to £100,000 or 10% of turnover (whichever higher) for security breach failures under 2022 Regulations
Criminal sanctions under Telecommunications Security Act 2021: Directors/persons responsible for significant security breaches can face criminal prosecution for non-compliance with security duties
Spectrum licence revocation: Ofcom can revoke or vary spectrum licences for non-compliance — effectively blocking service provision in that band
Forfeiture of apparatus: Under Communications Act Section 134, offensive/dangerous apparatus can be forfeited
NIS 2025 telecoms penalties: Up to £17,000,000 or 4% of qualifying turnover for NIS-combined security and reporting failures

PECR enforcement by ICO: Up to £500,000 (PECR cap) for nuisance calls, unsolicited electronic marketing, cookie consent failures. Note: ICO can use UK GDPR powers alongside for combined DPA/PECR breaches up to £17.5M
ICO enforcement (UK GDPR): Up to £17,500,000 or 4% of annual worldwide turnover for telecoms customer data breaches
Ofcom Consumer Protection Enforcement: Variation orders, suspension orders, compliance notices, enforcement under GCE conditions — escalating to financial penalty

Bereavement charges enforcement: Under Ofcom's 2024 enforcement initiative, providers must stop automatically charging for deceased customers' services; penalties for non-compliance (up to 10% turnover)
Ofcom compliance monitoring fee: Separate cost recovery fee for compliance monitoring work
Public naming: Ofcom publishes enforcement notifications and final penalty decisions in official notifications and public register
Competition law penalties: CMA/Ofcom concurrent competition powers under Competition Act 1998 — up to 30% of turnover for anti-competitive conduct in telecoms markets
